titleEn: Sport and Organisation Rules of the International Judo Federation: refereeing rules
readFrom: Explanatory_Guide_Judo_Referee-2026.pdf, the IJF's published explanatory guide carrying section D1.1 and Articles 1 to 21 of the refereeing rules
rights: Copyright in the rulebook is the International Judo Federation's. Nothing from it is transcribed here. Every technique that cites it carries a paraphrase written for this book and the article number the paraphrase came from, so a reader can check the claim against the IJF's own copy.

note.en: The refereeing rules change with the Olympic cycle, and a rule written down without its edition goes wrong quietly. Techniques cite this record by sourceId and article number rather than repeating the rulebook's name, so the next edition is one file to replace.
The referee's signals for every score, penalty and command, held for three to five seconds so the table can read them.

articlesCited.titleEn: Technique Coinciding with the Time Signal

note.en: A technique started in the last second counts; one applied after the signal does not; a hold-down started in regular time runs on past the signal until it scores or is broken.
Where the referee and the athletes stand, the bow, which is not compulsory, and the rule that athletes do not shake hands before the start.

What ends a contest and what wins it; golden score with no time limit and no rest, scores and shido carried over, won by any score, a third shido or hansoku-make, and a hold-down in golden score ending it at five seconds; the step back, the bow and leaving by the side of the mat with the judogi on.
The four criteria for ippon, and the rule that a voluntary bridge after being thrown scores ippon against the judoka who bridges.
What each score is given for, standing and on the ground.
When a hold-down counts, and the rule that it is never valid around the head and neck alone without control of at least one arm.

What a shido is given for: lack of combativity, an illegal move that is not dangerous, untidy attire or hair. Two are warnings and the third is hansoku-make; a shido never scores for the other athlete.

articlesCited.titleEn: Shido for a Lack of Combativity

note.en: Defensive posture, false attacks, forty-five seconds without an attack once conventional grips are taken, and stepping out of the area on purpose.
The leg grabs, the gripping restrictions, and standing joint locks and strangles at the lower degree of risk.
Throwing or defending with the head, and reverse seoi-nage, in cadet events only.
Diving forward onto the head while throwing.

articlesCited.titleEn: Hansoku-make for Acts against the Spirit of Judo

note.en: The techniques given a direct hansoku-make by name, the sankaku restrictions, and lifting an opponent off the mat to force them back down.
